class.name: WaterUnderwaterEffect
class.brief_description: Grades the frame while the camera is under a [WaterBody3D]: underwater fog, color and exposure, eased across the surface.
class.description:
Watches a camera against a [WaterBody3D] and, while it is below the water surface, swaps the scene's [WorldEnvironment] for a graded copy: the fog turns to [member water_color] at [member fog_density], and brightness, contrast and saturation ease to the underwater values. The grade interpolates in and out over [member transition_speed] instead of popping at the waterline.
Implemented with plain [Environment] properties, not a post-process pass, so it works on every renderer and composes with the surface's own below-water shading (Snell's window and total internal reflection, from the water material). It grades the whole frame, which is what being underwater looks like.
Needs a [WorldEnvironment] with an [Environment] in the scene. The environment is duplicated at runtime and the original is restored when the node leaves the tree. [signal submerged_changed] fires when the smoothed state crosses the surface: hook audio bus filters, camera effects or gameplay to it.

method.name: get_submersion
method.description: The smoothed underwater amount: 0 above water, 1 fully under. Use it to drive continuous effects; [method is_submerged] is the thresholded binary state.

method.name: is_submerged
method.description: [code]true[/code] while [method get_submersion] is above 0.5, i.e. the camera is (smoothed) under the water.

members.member: [Camera3D] to watch. Empty = the active camera of the viewport.
Fog density underwater, in the environment's fog units. The scene's own fog density is blended toward this.
How fast the grade follows the camera across the surface, in 1/s. 4 reaches the full grade in about a quarter second.
[WaterBody3D] to test the camera against. Required.
Fog color underwater: the water body's tint, which the scene fades toward as the camera goes under.

signal.name: submerged_changed
signal.description: Emitted when the camera crosses the surface (with the smoothing applied): [code]true[/code] going under, [code]false[/code] coming back up.
